name: social contact
description: There are many sensations created by encounters with other people. Each of us has a strategy for interacting with various groups that's built into our identities.
perceptions: I'm interacting with a person or people.
I have expectations about who I'm interacting with.
There are certain topics that are in-scope or out-of-scope for this context.

variations.name: friendly social contact
variations.description: Being amongst people perceived as likely to accept important aspects of your identity. Of course, there's a wide range of sensations within this category from old friends to warm strangers.
perceptions: I'm interacting with a person or people.
I expect this interaction to be low-stress.
There are certain topics that are in-scope or out-of-scope for this context.

variations.name: transactional social contact
variations.description: Expecting other people to just do their jobs with minimal social contact and not push unnecessary social discomfort into your day.
perceptions: I'm interacting with a person or people.
I expect this interaction to be quick and low-stress.
There are certain topics that are in-scope or out-of-scope for this context.
examples: the checkout person at the grocery store can chat about the weather but not about past medical problems

variations.name: unfriendly social contact
variations.description: A social encounter with a notable element of tension.
perceptions: I'm interacting with a person or people.
examples: encounter with someone who has wronged you
someone who makes you feel unsafe
stereotype of someone who might not like your kind of person

variations.name: anonymous social contact
variations.description: Being amongst others but not explicitly interacting with them. For example, 'people watching' is a kind of social contact even it's just reading body language and cultural signaling.
perceptions: I'm amongst people that I don't know.
We are not interacting directly, but are sharing a location and perhaps an activity.
examples: working on your laptop from the coffee shop

variations.name: foreign social contact
variations.description: Trying to communicate with a person who doesn't speak your language well. Difficulty in communicating intentions could lead to frustration, annoyance, humor, humility, or anything in-between.
perceptions: I'm interacting with a person or people.
We are not able to communicate freely with each other.
I need to understand them and to be understood.

guidance.description: Today, you’re more likely than ever before to meet, work with, live with, study with and maybe even fall in love with people with a different first language from you, who were brought up in a culture that’s different from your own. Communicating across language and culture barriers can be a recipe for confusion, frustration and causing offence, but with a bit of effort from both parties, it doesn’t have to be.

variations.name: utility contact
variations.description: Keeping in touch with someone mostly because that relationship brings status or could be beneficial in the future.
perceptions: Experiences with this person are neutral.
They have access to something that could be useful someday.
I'd like to maintain a relationship just in case.

guidance.description: Networking is a valuable skill that can help you advance your career, find new opportunities, and learn from others in your field. But networking is not a one-time event. It requires consistent and strategic follow-up to maintain and strengthen your connections.

examples: She knows about all the job openings in my industry.

commentaries.quote: We are deeply social creatures with a nuanced ability to perceive the social situation. Unless you're a psychopath, your social sense is as developed and important as your sense of smell.

We can choose what strategy we take when engaging in social contacts of different types: giving others the benefit of the doubt, assuming they're going to cheat us if possible, or just whatever our mood is at the moment.
Human interaction is something that I believe, as humans, we crave for. And that is where bars and social environments come into play.

We’re losing social skills, the human interaction skills, how to read a person’s mood, to read their body language, how to be patient until the moment is right to make or press a point. Too much exclusive use of electronic information dehumanizes what is a very, very important part of community life and living together.
commentaries.attribution: Vincent Nichols, Cardinal of the Roman Catholic Church

commentaries.quote: The person who is truly effective has the humility and reverence to recognize his own perceptual limitations and to appreciate the rich resources available through interaction with the hearts and minds of other human beings.
